thread:
Stephanie Nguyen: need a crisp explanation for a late-stage Dedicated deal: “burst capacity” vs just scaling their reserved GPUs. what can we promise + how to position it?

Markus Klein: +1. they’re asking if burst is basically autoscale-on-demand and if it guarantees headroom during product launches.

Simran Kaur: quick framing I’ve used:
- Reserved Dedicated = your baseline pool, always there, predictable throughput.
- Burst = temporary *paid* ability to go above baseline by borrowing from Redwood-managed burst pools in the same region/hardware class.
- Not a replacement for baseline sizing; it’s for spikes.

Lukas Meyer: what’s the simplest “when to recommend” rule of thumb?

Lauren Bishop: rule of thumb:
- If they exceed baseline frequently or it’s business-critical (always-on), increase reserved capacity.
- If spikes are predictable/periodic (weekly indexing, launches, batch jobs) and they don’t want to pay for idle GPUs the rest of the time, add burst.

Stephanie Nguyen: can we say “guaranteed burst” at all? they’re pushing for commitments.

Lauren Bishop: we should not say guaranteed in the generic sense.
Burst is governed by admission control + fleet safety caps to protect SLOs. Customers get:
- a configured burst limit (cap) and priority tier (where applicable)
- transparent denial reasons (e.g., cap reached, pool saturated, cooldown window)
But it’s not the same as reserving more baseline.

Markus Klein: can you give me a 2–3 sentence version I can drop in email?

Simran Kaur: draft:
“Dedicated Reserved capacity is your always-on baseline: fixed GPUs with predictable throughput. Burst is an add-on that lets you temporarily exceed that baseline by borrowing from Redwood-managed burst pools (same region/GPU class) during peak windows, billed only for what you use. Bursting is guarded by admission control and fleet safety limits, so it’s best for predictable spikes—not a substitute for right-sizing baseline when demand is sustained.”

Lukas Meyer: nice. add something about customer experience when denied (queue vs fail)?

Lauren Bishop: for GA we’re doing deterministic policy decision + explicit response signals. In practice:
- If burst is denied, routing/gateway will either apply backpressure (429/overload with retry hints) or route to baseline only (depends on endpoint + tenant policy).
- Customers can see denial reasons in Console + dashboards.
We shouldn’t promise “queueing always” because it varies by client + route.

Stephanie Nguyen: ok. any clean contrast bullets for the call?

Simran Kaur: bullets:
- Baseline (Reserved): guaranteed allocation, steady latency/throughput, priced as monthly commit.
- Burst: pay-per-use overage, good for short peaks, transparent limits/denials, protected by fairness + cooldown.
- If you need “always available extra,” reserve more baseline; burst is “elastic within guardrails.”

Markus Klein: prospect asked “what happens to other tenants if we burst?”

Lauren Bishop: answer: bursting is isolated via shared pool segmentation + fairness; plus SLO gates/circuit breakers to protect non-burst tenants. If fleet safety triggers, burst is reduced/disabled automatically.

Rishi Malhotra: from pricing POV: try to avoid “cheap overflow.” It’s priced as premium elasticity vs baseline commit economics. Message it as “operational flexibility” rather than discount.

Stephanie Nguyen: can we attach any artifact? (enablement one-pager?)

Lauren Bishop: use the enablement draft + docs snippet:
- go-to-market one-pager (draft): https://drive.google.com/…/burst-option-enablement-one-pager
- product doc (internal): https://confluence/…/dedicated-burst-option-packaging
For customers: we can share the external docs once the latest pass is merged (Elliot/Kira are polishing denial reason wording).

Lukas Meyer: any red flags / phrasing to avoid?

Simran Kaur: avoid:
- “unlimited burst”
- “guaranteed extra GPUs”
- “spot-like pricing”
Use:
- “configurable burst cap”
- “best-effort elasticity within SLO guardrails”
- “same-region burst pools”

Stephanie Nguyen: perfect. I’ll use Simran’s 3-sentence email + bullets for call. will ping if they push on guarantees.

Markus Klein: :thumbsup: thanks all
